scope: Wording pass under the 16 November 2026 rule: displayed texts name no dictionaries, studies, research authors or the Lithuanian language commission, and do not present a name as being of Russian origin. Display only; research modules keep their wording and provenance.
changes: Generators rewritten and rerun: round 133 (no commission intro, no “in its Russian form”), round 137 (no study, author, dictionary or portal), rounds 136/139 closing sentence (no “source known to us”), round 132 exact-form template (no “the dictionary records it”).
Estonian 1936/1929 recommended-name lists: the compiler’s name removed in all languages across the history modules (807 replacements); the lists themselves stay as historical publications.
Phonetic-formation template in namedays-content.js no longer says “the dictionary classifies”.

New display layer public/namedays-plain-r140.js: exact English research sentences are dropped or replaced with neutral five-language sentences at the same position; language-specific substring fixes cover translations that are not sentence-aligned. Applied to reviewed histories (plainHistory) and, newly, to hypotheses (plainHypothesis).

About 45 sentences that presented a name as Russian (e.g. “Kira is the Russian feminine form of Kir”, “Latvian Igors follows the Russian form”) now give the ultimate origin or a Slavic/neutral wording; cognate lists (“Russian Ivan, German Johannes”) and historical events stay.
Two tests updated to the new rule (the 1993 rendering-table sentence is no longer displayed); a rule test was added.
kept_on_purpose: Biographies of namesakes that mention dictionaries or studies (Elmar Muuk, Asta Laugalienė, Irēna), a 2016 study of St Erik’s bones, historical events involving Russia, cognate lists, and the 1929/1936 Estonian name lists as dated publications.
scan: English displayed texts: 9 remaining matches, all kept on purpose; non-English scans reviewed the same way (var/namedays-research/wording140*.mjs).
